description: AstroRelics is an interactive, real-time 3D web application designed to preserve and communicate the history of human space exploration through the lens of space archaeology. Rather than presenting static archive photos and 2D databases, our system places the user inside an interactive astronomical model spanning the Earth–Moon–Mars orbital corridor, mapping historical NASA hardware preserved across celestial surfaces and the deep space vacuum.
summary:
AstroRelics is an interactive 3D web experience dedicated to space archaeology across the Earth, Moon, and Mars orbital corridor. Built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, and custom GLSL shaders, the platform transforms static space history into a navigable astronomical environment. Users travel through smooth orbital transitions and inspect five iconic NASA artifacts: the Apollo 12 Saturn V third stage (J002E3), the Apollo 11 LRRR laser retroreflector, the Apollo 10 Snoopy lunar module, the Opportunity rover, and the Ingenuity helicopter, each anchored to real geographic coordinates or drifting in deep space.

Instead of relying on flat 2D archives or dense tables, AstroRelics addresses the challenge of making complex space telemetry, orbital mechanics, and mission history engaging and accessible. Users can explore 360° 3D models, examine engineering specifications, and complete interactive archive investigation missions (Echoes of Space).

This is important because humanity’s artifacts beyond Earth are not mere space debris. They are irreplaceable historical monuments and active scientific instruments. By turning space heritage into an immersive educational journey, AstroRelics bridges aerospace data and storytelling to preserve the legacy of human space exploration
details:
What It Does and How It Works AstroRelics is an interactive 3D web platform dedicated to space archaeology across the Earth, Moon, and Mars corridor. When the application launches, an automated preloader normalizes all .glb 3D models by computing bounding boxes and centering pivots while displaying an animated astrolabe loading screen. Once inside, users navigate freely between celestial bodies through mathematically calculated orbital transitions and a hyperspace visual effect. Surface artifacts, including the Apollo 11 LRRR retroreflector at Mare Tranquillitatis, the Opportunity rover at Meridiani Planum, and the Ingenuity helicopter at Jezero Crater, are positioned using spherical projection from real latitude and longitude coordinates onto 3D planetary meshes. Deep space relics, such as the Apollo 12 Saturn V third stage (J002E3) and the Apollo 10 Snoopy lunar module, are placed in orbital space. Selecting any planet or relic enables 360° 3D inspection alongside a telemetry drawer with engineering specifications, mission history, scientific impact, and interactive archive investigation missions (Echoes of Space).

Benefits and Intended Impact Traditional space archives often rely on static 2D photographs and dense technical tables that lack spatial scale. AstroRelics transforms these records into an intuitive, browser based exploration tool that requires no downloads or specialized hardware. Our intended impact is to democratize space heritage and inspire students, educators, and curious minds by showing that spacecraft left beyond Earth are not mere debris, but lasting monuments of human ingenuity and active scientific instruments.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used

  • Languages and Core Framework: TypeScript, React 18, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, and Vite.
  • 3D Graphics and Shaders: Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, and custom GLSL shaders for Rayleigh atmospheric scattering, Fresnel halos, and procedural starfields and nebulae.
  • Audio and Interface: Native Web Audio API for procedural sound synthesis, Lucide React icons, custom vector illustrations, and full bilingual support in English and Portuguese.
  • Scientific Sources: Mission parameters, coordinates, and historical records based on documented data from NASA, JPL, CNEOS, and ILRS.

Creativity and Design Considerations Our creativity lies in blending rigorous scientific telemetry with atmospheric storytelling. Each celestial body features tailored visual physics: Earth displays a blue Rayleigh atmosphere with a twilight terminator, the Moon uses high roughness regolith materials with no atmosphere to emphasize the vacuum, and Mars features a thin carbon dioxide Fresnel glow. Beyond free exploration, the Echoes of Space mode turns real historical mysteries, such as the 33 year disappearance of J002E3, into an interactive investigation. Throughout development, we prioritized scientific accuracy, smooth camera pathing that prevents planetary collisions, responsive design across desktop and mobile screens, and a resilient compatibility screen for devices without WebGL acceleration.
dataRefs: NASA JPL Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS)
